turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Hello, am I speaking with Mr. Gupta from Pune?

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: Yes, this is Gupta speaking. Who is this calling?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Namaste sir, I am Anjali from the State Bank security team. I am calling just to confirm a transaction of nine thousand five hundred rupees made on your account today.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: Oh, yes, I did that for my grandson's books. Is there some problem?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: No sir, everything is fine and the payment was successful. I am calling because we noticed a new device login, so we wanted to ensure it was you.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: I did change my phone last week. Does that mean my account is not safe?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: It is safe, sir. But please remember that the bank will never call you to ask for your password or OTP to verify anything.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: But if you are from the bank, you might need some details to check?

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: Never, Mr. Gupta. Please never share your PIN or any OTP with anyone over the phone, even if they claim to be from the bank.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: I see. I was a bit worried when the phone rang.

turns.speaker: caller
turns.text: It is better to be cautious. Just ignore any one who asks for your Aadhaar or card numbers over a call.

turns.speaker: receiver
turns.text: Thank you for the warning, beta. I will keep this in mind.
